overview:
SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH. My lab's long-term research mission is to elucidate the mechanisms underlying selective vulnerability in neurological and psychiatric disorders, with a focus on identifying the transcriptional programs which define neuronal identity and mitochondrial function. The majority of my lab’s recently published work has focused on determining how transcriptional dysfunction contributes to the generation of abnormal neuronal function and behavior in models of Parkinson Disease (PD), Huntington Disease, and schizophrenia. 

TRAINING AND MENTORSHIP. Throughout my career, I have been extensively involved in undergraduate and graduate training. I have directly mentored eight graduate students and fifty undergraduate researchers, and I have served on thesis committees of 45 additional students. In my current role as the Associate Director for Training in the Center for Neurodegeneration and Experimental Therapeutics at UAB, I am working to enhance the training experiences of graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and undergraduate students in neurodegeneration by providing career development opportunities and building a structure for inter-lab and interdepartmental collaborations and activities. 

DRUG DISCOVERY AND DEVELOPMENT. In my role as Chair of Neuroscience at Southern Research (2017-2022), I coordinated neuroscience drug discovery efforts and facilitated interactions with faculty at Southern Research and UAB and with other external clients. Back at UAB, I have been charged with assisting the neuroscience community with re-envisioning their ongoing projects to incorporate strategies for target identification, prioritization, and validation, with the goal of identifying good candidates for moving into a neurodegeneration drug discovery pipeline with Southern Research.
